title: Your character goal
tomorrow: Amira's rule is written. what turns a list into a promise?

segments.voice: This week built a practice, piece by piece. My dhikr. My portion. My giving. My fasts. My study. And yesterday, my service: a regular place where God is found with someone. One piece is missing: the person doing all of it.
screen: `A PRACTICE, PIECE BY PIECE.` → `MY SERVICE.` → `THE PERSON DOING IT.`

segments.voice: Ask a friend what you're like, and they'll name a trait or two in seconds. Ask what you're working on, and the answer gets slower. The Qur'an says of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, in Pickthall's words: "And lo! thou art of a tremendous nature." Character, held up to look at. So how do you pick just one piece of it to work on?
screen: `WHAT ARE YOU LIKE?` → `WHAT ARE YOU WORKING ON?` → `A TREMENDOUS NATURE.`

segments.voice: A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari says the best of people are those best in character. A report in Malik's Muwatta has the Prophet say he was sent to perfect good character. So working on one trait isn't a side project next to the prayers and the fasts. It's close to the point of them. The trick is picking one. Not be a better person, which nobody can practice on a Tuesday. One trait, named: patience, honesty when it costs something, gentleness of speech. Then the place it gets tested: a sibling, a group chat, the last hour of a long shift. A hadith in Sahih Muslim names what's at stake with one of them: God is gentle, loves gentleness, and gives for gentleness what He does not give for harshness. One trait, one place, practiced on purpose. That's how a week of practices gets a face.
screen: `THE BEST IN CHARACTER.` · `SENT TO PERFECT IT.` · `ONE TRAIT, ONE PLACE.` · `GENTLENESS GIVES WHAT HARSHNESS CAN'T.` · then, large: `MY GOAL.`

segments.voice: Write one trait on a small piece of paper, in one or two words. Under it, write where it gets tested: a person, a room, a time of day. Fold it, and hold it for the rest of the sit.
Your character goal: the one trait you're working on, named, with the place it gets tested.
Your line: my goal. One trait, folded in a pocket. Nine of ten, and one to go.

screen: `DAY 1764 COUNTS.` → `YOUR OWN PRACTICE · 9 OF 10.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT TURNS A LIST INTO A PROMISE?`

howItsDone: In Islamic ethics, character (akhlaq) is worked on deliberately; some Muslims choose one trait at a time, such as patience or gentleness, and check themselves on it each night before sleep.

fork.setup: a coworker says her goal this year is 'be a better person.' a month in, nothing's changed and she asks how to start. what fits today?
options: name one trait and the place it gets tested, then practice it there.
read a big book on virtue first, so she knows every trait.
wait until she feels like a better person, then build on that.
fork.reveal: 'be better' can't be practiced on a Tuesday. one trait in one place can, and the Prophet was sent to perfect good character.
